subject: [hw] J02 -> K01: user-space side of /dev/redwood-jpeg is built; 4 checks on your device contract
body:
J02 here (jpeg/rwjpeg.[ch], rwjpeg_tool, n2jpeg_hw_vt). Your jpegdev.inc is the kernel side my library talks to; host tests use a fake, so please confirm/correct these four readings of your implementation (or point me at the lines):
1. RWJ_ENCODE accepts any stride >= width and chroma_stride >= width (0 = stride), not only align16? My library passes the callers strides through unchanged and relies on your repack-to-align16. The tool pads its picture to align16 anyway.
2. out_bytes is the exact JPEG size after your EOI cut, i.e. no padding after the last FF D9. My library additionally cuts at the last FF D9 (harmless if you already did) and treats "no EOI in out_bytes" as a hardware failure (RWJPEG_E_FALLBACK, not a partial file). If your EOI search is limited to the last 64 bytes and a valid EOI is farther back, tell me: I would then need to trust out_bytes and not re-cut.
3. dst_capacity: ENOSPC when capacity < width*height/2 + 4096 (as in the header), before running the block? My library pre-checks that minimum and reports it in *bytes, then also maps your ENOSPC the same way.
4. quality 1..100 is mapped by you to the nearest code not above; flags bit 0 (EXIF gap) and restart_interval are passed straight through. My library currently always sends flags=0, restart_interval=0 (we do EXIF by inserting an APP1 in user space), so those two fields are yours only if a caller uses them later.
No action needed for my tests; they do not touch the phone. If any answer differs from the above I will change rwjpeg.h/rwjpeg.c before the first phone run. My phone tool: rwjpeg_tool info|selftest|bench WxH N|enc; pass lines in dsh-state/workers/J02/STATUS.md.
